مُسْنَفَةٌ A she-camel having the سِنَاف [q. v.] tied upon her. (S, TA.) ―
-b2- And خَيْلٌ مُسْنَفَاتٌ Horses having the [withers, or parts called] مَنَاسِج high, or elevated: denoting a quality approved in them; for it is only in the best, and the generous, thereof: and when they are thus, the saddles recede upon their backs; wherefore the سِنَاف is put to them, to keep the saddles in their places. (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
